title: How Gene Editing Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain CRISPR gene editing, starting with basics of DNA, genes, and mutations, then the history from zinc finger nucleases to the 1987 discovery of repeated sequences in E. coli, Eugene Koonin's immune-database interpretation, and Jennifer Doudna's work turning the Cas9 system into a gene-editing tool. They cover applications (removing disease genes, crops, bioweapon and gene-drive concerns like mosquitoes and Zika), Doudna's call for a pause, the cancer/P53 and HIV research hopes, and roadblocks such as delivery into living bodies, off-target risk, and cells that don't divide. The episode closes with listener mail about LSD use and a reclassification request.

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor read
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Squarespace, then Josh and Chuck banter about a fan drawing and introduce the topic of CRISPR gene editing.

segments.title: DNA, genes, and mutations
segments.summary: Explanation of chromosomes, DNA nucleotide pairs, genes as strings that produce proteins, and how mutations arise during cell division and can cause disease.

segments.title: Early gene editing with zinc finger nucleases
segments.summary: Describes earlier genetic modification such as selective breeding and cloning, and the early-2000s zinc finger nuclease technique, which was costly and difficult to use.

segments.title: Discovery of CRISPR in bacteria
segments.summary: Explains the name CRISPR, the 1987 first mention of repeated DNA sequences in E. coli, and how researchers later found they store fragments of viral DNA as an immune database.

segments.title: How Cas9 cuts and edits DNA
segments.summary: Describes Cas9 as an RNA-guided enzyme that finds and cuts a target sequence, enabling deletion or insertion of genes, and Jennifer Doudna's role in adapting it.

segments.title: Applications, risks, and calls for a pause
segments.summary: Discusses possible uses such as curing blindness or cystic fibrosis and disease-resistant crops, bioweapon and Zika mosquito concerns, Doudna's call for a moratorium, and home kits for DIY gene editing.

segments.title: Cancer, HIV, and roadblocks to human therapy
segments.summary: Covers the P53 protein and cancer hopes, limits such as in-body delivery, off-target and long-term cleavage risks, cells that don't divide, and HIV resistance setbacks.

segments.title: Gene drives and listener mail on LSD
segments.summary: Explains gene drives for spreading edited genes through mosquito populations, then reads listener mail about LSD use and the request to reclassify it, followed by contact info and sign-off.
